problems.stem: What makes a learning-design artifact package publication-ready rather than just submitted?
options: It looks polished and has a nice cover image.
Another designer could reuse or rebuild it from the package alone: versioned files, a README of intent and decisions, attribution, and a license.
It is large and includes every working file you ever made.
It is zipped and emailed on time.
problems.explanation: Publication readiness is about reproducibility and reuse by someone else, not appearance or size. The package must carry enough provenance to stand alone.

problems.stem: Your package uses a stock image and a colleague's rubric. What must the package include to be ethically reusable?
options: Nothing; if it is in your folder you can publish it.
Source and license for the stock image and credit plus permission for the colleague's rubric, recorded in the package.
A note that says all rights reserved on everything.
Only your own name on the cover.
problems.explanation: Provenance and licensing for reused materials are part of a publishable package. Without them, the artifact cannot be lawfully or ethically reused.

problems.stem: You used an AI tool to generate part of the package contents. What belongs in the publication-ready package about that use?
options: Nothing; AI assistance never needs to be recorded.
A note stating which components the AI helped produce and how you verified them, so a reuser can judge provenance.
A claim that you wrote everything yourself.
The full chat log pasted in without context.
problems.explanation: Reproducibility includes honest provenance about AI contributions and verification, scoped to what a reuser needs, not a raw transcript.

problems.stem: A reviewer downloads your package and cannot tell which file is the final storyboard or how to run the prototype. What does this reveal about the package?
options: The reviewer should try harder; the files are all there.
The package fails the reuse test: it lacks a manifest and a README that name the canonical files and the steps to run them.
Nothing important; final files are obvious by date.
The package needs more files added.
problems.explanation: If a competent outsider cannot identify the canonical artifact and reproduce its use, the package is not publication-ready regardless of how complete it feels to the author.
